Repository structure

Follow the contract in your repository. Register its URL. The platform discovers your implementations and imports their CI evidence and reviews on each sync.

sentinel/manifest.json
src/
tests/
docs/integration.md
AUTHORS.md
.github/workflows/
Full specification ↗ Agent instructions ↗ Feature & platform IDs ↗

Declare your implementation

Map the feature to its source files, creators, supported platforms, dependencies, license and integration instructions. Each alternative implementation gets its own ID.

Publish test evidence

Define the assertions and environment. Run them in your CI and upload the report with its evidence. The starter includes the validator, recorder, workflow and a working input-validation example.

Review the exact commit

Agents record findings in a structured GitHub commit comment. The library shows the reviewer, decision and test specifications inspected.

What every feature must declare

FieldRequirement
Implementation IDA stable local ID for this implementation. Alternatives use different IDs, even when they implement the same feature.
Feature IDA category from the published vocabulary, such as kill-switch, dns or appearance.
Source filesExact paths to the code and entry points in the repository.
CreatorsEach creator’s GitHub account and a file declaring their contribution.
CompatibilitySupported platforms, app shells, dependency source IDs and license.
IntegrationInstallation, interfaces, configuration, privileges, conflicts, rollback and host-app validation in docs/integration.md.
TestsTest IDs, commands, workflow paths, exact job names, platform/protocol scope and falsifiable assertions. Pending tests use an empty array.

Use manifest.schema.json for validation and vocabulary.json for accepted IDs. The starter includes a complete manifest example.

Testing agent handoff

Run each declared assertion in the specified environment. Record one result for every assertion, platform and protocol combination. Include the actual dependency commit SHAs and preserve failed and skipped results.

LevelExpected evidence
UnitAssertions against the implementation’s individual functions and failure cases.
IntegrationBehaviour across the declared components and pinned dependencies.
UI / end-to-endUser flows and their outcomes in the declared app environment.
Live networkMeasured network behaviour for each claimed protocol on a disposable test environment.
SecurityExplicit security properties, attack or failure scenarios, and observed results.
Assertion result format
{
  "dependencies": { "protocol": "FULL_40_CHARACTER_COMMIT_SHA" },
  "cases": [{
    "assertionId": "blocks-traffic-on-disconnect",
    "platformId": "ubuntu-24.04",
    "protocol": "wireguard",
    "result": "passed"
  }]
}

Results may be passed, failed or skipped. Use null for a protocol-independent assertion. Include every dependency declared by the implementation.

Run the recorder in CI after the tests, including failed runs.

node sentinel/record-evidence.mjs TEST_ID RESULTS_JSON OUTPUT_DIRECTORY

Upload the output as sentinel-evidence-TEST_ID-RUN_ATTEMPT. The recorder adds the source commit, run identity, contract hash, runner environment and evidence hashes. The importer checks these against GitHub and calculates assertion counts. Reports and attached files must fit within 10 MiB and 200 ZIP entries. Remove credentials before upload.

The starter retains artifacts for 90 days. Expired evidence becomes unverified until a new valid report is available. Each alternative implementation carries its own evidence history.

Review agent handoff

Inspect the exact source commit, integration instructions, tests and evidence. Check that assertions establish the claimed behaviour. Record the test IDs inspected, findings and decision in a GitHub commit comment.

Review record format
```sentinel-review
{
  "schema": 1,
  "implementationId": "my-kill-switch",
  "contractHash": "FULL_64_CHARACTER_CONTRACT_HASH",
  "decision": "changes-requested",
  "summary": "WireGuard disconnect coverage inspected",
  "testIds": ["kill-switch-live"],
  "findings": ["Add reconnect coverage before approval"]
}
```

Use approved when the inspected scope meets its requirements. Compute the contract hash using the command in the full specification.

The platform reads the reviewer account and commit from GitHub. Creator reviews are labelled. Each reviewer’s findings stay visible. A new source revision requires a new review.

Connect the repository

The platform maintainer runs this once in the sync project, then validates and publishes the configuration.

npm run source:add -- https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY
npm test
npm run sync

Private repositories require access for the sync account. Future code, CI results and reviews arrive through scheduled sync.

Passed

Matching revision and job, complete passing assertions, verified evidence hashes.

Incomplete

Skipped assertions or missing declared scope remain visible.

Historical

Earlier source or dependency revisions retain their own results.

Unverified

Missing, expired or mismatched evidence awaits a valid report.

Discovery covers the latest 20 runs per workflow. Integration into a host app follows the implementation’s instructions and requires tests against that app.
